title: A clearer view of tomorrow
text: Welcome to Wind Desk, a pilot for the Great Britain day-ahead electricity team. This portal brings together two questions: what wind forecast did we have when we made our decision, and how much error should we understand around that forecast? Everything you see comes from the requested Elexon wind forecast and wind outturn datasets. The pilot covers decisions made from January first through January thirty first, twenty twenty six, with next-day delivery. The data is archived and the product is a research pilot, rather than a live trading feed.

title: The forecast you actually had
text: Here we are making a decision on January fifteenth at nine fifty London time, for delivery on January sixteenth. The average eligible wind forecast is seven thousand nine hundred and seventy five megawatts. The teal curve shows the latest forecast available for each delivery hour at that cutoff. The dashed curve shows actual generation retrospectively. Those actuals were not known at decision time. Change the decision date or cutoff to explore a different information set. The default cutoff is an explicit N two E X auction assumption. An operational desk should allow additional time for ingestion, analysis and order entry.

title: Quantify the uncertainty
text: Across the full January decision cohort at the default cutoff, all seven hundred and forty four expected hourly pairs are available. Mean absolute error is about two thousand and thirteen megawatts. Root mean squared error is about two thousand five hundred and six megawatts, emphasizing the larger misses. Signed bias is positive one thousand seven hundred and thirty megawatts. Positive means wind was over-forecast, which may create replacement energy exposure. Weighted absolute percentage error is seventeen point eight four percent. The performance view shows how daily mean errors vary, so the month average does not hide the changing pattern.

title: Turn evidence into a better discussion
text: For this selected delivery day, positive hourly wind gaps sum to about fifteen thousand and sixty four megawatt hours. That is realised national wind shortfall, not a purchase order for your portfolio. The historical ninetieth percentile shortfall uses only earlier delivery days. It is a reference from a small growing sample, not a calibrated prediction interval. The expandable audit trail shows publication timestamps and forecast age, and Export day provides the underlying hourly comparison. To turn this pilot into a procurement product, the next step is to combine portfolio exposure, customer demand and contracted supply, then evaluate operational latency and economic outcomes.

title: A small, inspectable architecture
bullets: React + Vite: controls, charts, audit trail, CSV
FastAPI: validated analysis and export endpoints
Archived Elexon JSON: raw vintages + provenance hashes
Docker: one origin | Vercel: static UI + Python function
text: Now for the technical review. The React and Vite frontend handles controls, charts and presentation. Fast A P I validates requests and exposes analysis, health and CSV endpoints. A small immutable Elexon snapshot makes the pilot reproducible and keeps external API failures out of interactive requests. Raw files are preserved with source URLs, row counts and S H A two fifty six hashes. Parsed data is cached per Python process. There is no database because this is a fixed historical cohort. Docker builds the frontend in a Node stage and serves it beside Python in a non-root runtime. Vercel deploys the static frontend and Python function separately on the same origin.

title: Prevent look-ahead leakage
bullets: Filter target to next-day delivery window
Choose latest eligible publication per target
Join hourly forecast to two complete actual half-hours
Exclude missing pairs; reject conflicting duplicates
text: The main correctness boundary is in backend slash analysis dot py. For each target hour in the next-day delivery window, selection filters publication time to less than or equal to the decision cutoff, then takes the latest eligible row. Later revisions are never allowed into the historical forecast. The downloaded forecasts are hourly, while actuals are half-hourly. Both actual half-hours must exist, and their mean is compared to the hourly forecast. Missing pairs reduce coverage instead of becoming zero generation. Conflicting duplicate values fail explicitly. January thirty first decisions correctly include February first delivery. London and U T C coincide throughout this cohort.

title: Metrics with explicit limits
bullets: MAE / RMSE / bias / WAPE on paired hours
Sum positive hourly error -> MWh shortfall
P90 history: earlier delivery dates only
Retrospective actuals are not historical data vintages
text: Metrics are pure Python functions. Error is forecast minus actual. Mean absolute error, root mean squared error, signed bias and weighted absolute percentage error are calculated only on matched observations. A zero actual denominator produces an unavailable percentage. Positive errors summed over one-hour intervals produce megawatt hours. The historical shortfall reference uses nearest rank and only delivery dates before the selected decision date. This avoids using later delivery outcomes, but actual publication latency and revision vintages are not reconstructed. Therefore this is not a strict operational backtest of actual data availability. National operationally visible wind also cannot be assumed to match the client's renewable portfolio.

title: Verification and handover
bullets: 6 tests passed: cutoff, missingness, metrics, dates, API
React production build and deployed browser checked
README: setup, architecture, sources, AI disclosure
Docker included; engine unavailable for execution
Next: durable ingestion, portfolio mapping, monitoring
text: Six tests pass, covering the exact cutoff boundary and future revision exclusion, missing half-hours, metric signs and units, January and February boundaries, the historical sample filter, API input validation and CSV export. The React production build passes and the deployed interface and API have been checked. Docker configuration is included, but the execution machine has no Docker engine, so no container build is claimed. The README documents startup, deployment, file structure, assumptions, findings and limitations. Open A I Codex assisted research, implementation, documentation and verification. This video uses synthetic narration and captured application screens. Production follow-up should add durable ingestion, availability timestamps, monitoring, authenticated access and portfolio mapping. Thank you for reviewing Wind Desk.
